ghs.en: Misato: "Ah..."

rows.jp: 先輩の下肢を（今度は下心なく）白日にさらした時。
rows.en: When I bared Miyasumi’s leg to the light of day—without an ulterior motive this time—

ghs.en: Time to bring Senpai's lower extremities to the light (this time without ulterior motives).
ghs.assessment: The source is a temporal subordinate clause: 'When I exposed Senpai's lower limbs to the light...' The English turns it into a malformed declaration that it is time to act.
ghs.remedy: Use 'When I exposed Senpai's lower legs to the light...'

rows.jp: 出血している部位……に……歯形を見た。
rows.en: There... at the site of the bleeding... I saw teeth marks.

ghs.en: In... the part that is bleeding... I saw toothmarks.

rows.jp: 少量の血液が薄く広がり赤い湿気を与えている傷口の、周囲。
rows.en: They circled the wound, filmed with a thin red sheen of blood.

ghs.en: All around the mouth of the wound where a tiny amount of blood was creating a thinly spreading red moisture.

rows.jp: 何者かが、傷口を食いちぎろうとしたようにも見える。
rows.en: It looked as though something had tried to tear a chunk from the wound with its teeth.

ghs.en: It looks as if someone or something wanted to bite off the mouth of that wound.
ghs.assessment: The source's ようにも見える permits an inference that something tried to perform the action. The narrower defect is wanted to bite off the wound, which substitutes an internal desire and makes the wound itself the object to be bitten off.
ghs.remedy: Say that it looked as though something had tried to bite or tear at the wound.

rows.jp: いや。

ghs.en: No.

rows.jp: そうとしか、見えまい。
rows.en: There was no other possible conclusion.

ghs.en: What else could it even look like...
Taichi: "...Senpai?"

rows.jp: 「はい？」

ghs.en: Misato: "Yes?"

rows.jp: 「……軽蔑、しましたか？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...did you... despise...?"

rows.jp: 「軽蔑？」

ghs.en: Misato: "Despise?"

rows.jp: 「その」

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's,"

rows.jp: 言葉にならない。

ghs.en: Language that doesn't become words.
ghs.assessment: The English is incoherent and changes the first-person inability into an abstract statement about language. The source says he cannot put it into words.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I can't put it into words.'

rows.jp: 自分でさえ、うまく翻訳できない行動と気持ちを、どう釈明したらいいのか。
rows.en: How could I explain actions and feelings I could not even translate for myself?

ghs.en: How should I even explain acts and feelings that I cannot translate well, not even to myself?

rows.jp: 「だから」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I mean,"

rows.jp: 先輩がふっと微笑む。
rows.en: She gave me a faint smile.

ghs.en: Senpai puffs into a smile.
ghs.assessment: The source says Senpai smiles softly or suddenly. 'Puffs into' describes neither the motion nor the expression and creates an unsupported physical image.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Senpai smiles softly.'

rows.jp: 「軽蔑するようなことは、なにもしてませんよ、あなたは」
rows.en: “You haven’t done anything that would make me despise you.”

ghs.en: Misato: "You did nothing that is worthy of despise, you did not."
ghs.assessment: The complement is ungrammatical and the doubled ending is a literal calque. The source reassures him that he has done nothing she would despise.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You haven't done anything I'd despise you for.'

rows.jp: 「……そう、ですか？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...I... did not?"

rows.jp: だって。

ghs.en: But...

rows.jp: 傷口を見る。

ghs.en: I look at the cut.

rows.jp: 先輩はそっとスカートで覆う。
rows.en: She gently covered it with her skirt.

ghs.en: Senpai quietly covers it with the skirt.

rows.jp: 「おりこうさんなので、不問とします」
rows.en: “You’ve been a good boy, so I’ll let the matter drop.”

ghs.en: Misato: "You are a well-behaved kid, so I shall overlooking all that."
ghs.assessment: A modal auxiliary must take the base verb. The source says she will let the matter pass because he was good.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I shall overlook it.'

rows.jp: 「部活、手伝ってくれましたし」
rows.en: “Besides, you helped me with the club.”

ghs.en: Misato: "And you have been helping with club activities."
Taichi: "..."

rows.jp: 「手当、させてください」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Please allow me to care for that."
Misato: "...yes."

rows.jp: そして俺は、先輩の手当をした。
rows.en: And so I tended to Miyasumi’s injuries.

ghs.en: And then I gave medical care to Senpai.

rows.jp: 今度は、発作も起こらなかった。
rows.en: This time, there was no episode.

ghs.en: This time, no seizure occurred.

rows.jp: 嬉しかったから。

ghs.en: Because I was happy.

rows.jp: より上位の感情が、あったから。
rows.en: Because a stronger feeling had taken its place.

ghs.en: Because... that high-ranking emotion was there.
ghs.assessment: The source describes a higher-order or more powerful emotion. 'High-ranking' incorrectly treats the feeling as occupying an official rank.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Because there was a higher-order emotion.'

rows.jp: 「くすぐったいですー」

ghs.en: Misato: "That tickleees!"
ghs.assessment: The demonstrative subject requires a third-person singular verb. The elongated spelling can preserve delivery, but the verb lacks agreement.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That tickleees!'

rows.jp: 「ご、ごめんなさい……緊張して」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I, I am sorry... nervousness."
ghs.assessment: The English leaves an isolated noun and omits the predicate. The source apologizes and explains that he is nervous.
ghs.remedy: Use 'S-sorry... I'm nervous.'

rows.jp: 「包帯まくのへたっぴですねー」

ghs.en: Misato: "You are crap at making bandages are you."
ghs.assessment: The sentence is ungrammatical, and the source criticizes his skill at wrapping a bandage, not making bandages.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You're really bad at wrapping bandages, aren't you?'

highlights.text: crap at making bandages are you

rows.jp: 「経験なくて……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I am inexperienced..."

rows.jp: 「く、くすぐったい～っ」

ghs.en: Misato: "It-, it tickleee～s!!!"

rows.jp: 「うううう～……」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Nggg～h..."

rows.jp: そんな幸せな時間が。

ghs.en: That hours of this blessed happiness,
ghs.assessment: The source refers to such a happy time in the singular. The English has incompatible demonstrative and number marking and adds an unsupported 'blessed.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Such a happy time...'

highlights.text: That hours of this blessed happiness

rows.jp: あったんだ―――

ghs.en: would even exist---
ghs.assessment: The source completes the recollection with the factual past 'there was.' The English changes it into a hypothetical or future-in-the-past claim.
ghs.remedy: Use '...really existed—'

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah!"
ghs.assessment: The canonical source assigns the exclamation to Misato. The English speaker label instead gives it to Taichi, disrupting the following exchange.
ghs.remedy: Assign the line to Misato.

rows.jp: 「はい？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yes?"

rows.jp: 「わたしの携帯はどこです？」

ghs.en: Misato: "My cellphone, where is it?"

rows.jp: 「携帯、ですか？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Your cellphone...?"

rows.jp: 唐突な日常の言葉。
rows.en: A word from ordinary life, abrupt and jarring.

ghs.en: Sudden everyday words.

rows.jp: 思考が麻痺した。

ghs.en: It paralyzed thoughts.
ghs.assessment: The source says the narrator's thinking went numb or froze. The English invents an external 'it' as agent and uses an unnatural plural object.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My thoughts froze.'

rows.jp: 「落としたみたいです」

ghs.en: Misato: "It seems I have dropped it."

rows.jp: ひどく困った顔をする。

ghs.en: She makes a horribly worried face.

rows.jp: 「探してきます。きっと屋上だ」
rows.en: “I’ll find it. It must be on the roof.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I will go look. It has to be on the rooftop."

rows.jp: 「お願いします」

ghs.en: Misato: "Please do..."

rows.jp: 保健室を出て、屋上に向かった。
rows.en: I left the infirmary and headed for the roof.

ghs.en: I left the infirmary and headed towards the rooftop.

rows.jp: 携帯はすぐに見つかった。
rows.en: I found the phone almost at once.

ghs.en: I found the cellphone right away.

rows.jp: 散乱した資材の間に、転がっていた。
rows.en: It lay among the scattered materials.

ghs.en: It had fallen down when the pile of materials fell.
ghs.assessment: The source says the phone was lying among the scattered materials. The English invents a pile, a fall, and a causal time relation that the sentence does not state.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It was lying among the scattered materials.'

highlights.text: had fallen down when the pile of materials fell

rows.jp: 「どうして携帯なんて」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Why the cellphone, even."

rows.jp: 些細な疑問。

ghs.en: A trifling question.

rows.jp: 「いや」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Nah."

rows.jp: すぐにうち消す。

ghs.en: I immediately drown it out.

rows.jp: 誰だって、何かに頼っているはずだ。

ghs.en: Anybody would have something they rely on.

rows.jp: 俺がそうしているように、先輩もまたちっぽけな携帯電話に、大きなものを託しているのかもしれない。
rows.en: Just as I do, perhaps Miyasumi has entrusted something immense to that tiny phone.

ghs.en: Just like what I do, so Senpai might just be entrusting something great to this tiny little portable telephone.
ghs.assessment: The comparative construction is ungrammatical. The source says Senpai may entrust something important to her small phone just as the narrator relies on something himself.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Just as I do, Senpai may also be entrusting something important to that tiny phone.'

highlights.text: Just like what I do, so

rows.jp: 「これですよね」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Here it is!"

rows.jp: 「ああ、それ」

ghs.en: Misato: "Ahhh, it is!"

rows.jp: 破顔一笑、受け取る先輩。
rows.en: Her whole face lit up as she took it.

ghs.en: Senpai accepts it, smiling broadly.

rows.jp: 「ご苦労様。これでチャラですね」

ghs.en: Misato: "I very much appreciate it. With this, your debt is forgiven."
ghs.assessment: The source says the exchange makes them even or wipes the slate clean. The English imposes a one-way creditor-debtor relation and has Senpai forgive his debt.
ghs.remedy: Use 'With this, we're even.'

ghs.en: Taichi: "Eh...?"

rows.jp: 笑いきれずに、顔が歪む。
rows.en: My face twisted in a smile I couldn’t finish.

ghs.en: My face distorted, without even fully smiling,

rows.jp: 悪い冗談を聞いたようだ。
rows.en: As if I had just heard a sick joke.

ghs.en: as if I had just heard a bad joke.

rows.jp: 「ずいふん、あっさり許してくれるんですね」

ghs.en: Taichi: "That is... really a quick forgiveness there."

rows.jp: 「わたしだって群青なわけですし」

ghs.en: Misato: "I am an Ultramarine of Gunjou myself."

rows.jp: 「それに、またしますか？」
rows.en: “Besides... do you think you’ll do it again?”

ghs.en: Misato: "And so, will you be doing that again?"

rows.jp: 「……わかりません。可能性はありますよ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...I do not know. There is the possibility."
ghs.assessment: The recurrence possibility is preserved, but There is the possibility is an unidiomatic definite-noun calque in this exchange.
ghs.remedy: Use It's possible.

rows.jp: 「発作みたいなものですから」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Because it is something like a seizure."

rows.jp: 「じゃあ情状酌量の余地はあるわけですよ」

ghs.en: Misato: "Then there is room for leniency given the extenuating circumstances."
Taichi: "...naive."
Misato: "Eh?"

rows.jp: 「みみ先輩は、甘いな」
rows.en: “You’re way too soft on me, Mimi.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Mimi-senpai, you're naive."

rows.jp: 「俺は安全な年下の男なんかじゃない」

ghs.en: Taichi: "I ain't some harmless younger man."

rows.jp: 「でもやめてって言ったらやめてくれましたし」
rows.en: “But you stopped when I asked you to.”

ghs.en: Misato: "But when I told you to stop, you did stop."

rows.jp: そうなのか？

ghs.en: Did I now?

rows.jp: 言葉を解することもないはずなのに。
rows.en: Words should have meant nothing in that state.

ghs.en: But I expect I wouldn't have been able to interpret language.

rows.jp: 偶然？

ghs.en: Coincidence?

rows.jp: そうに決まってる。

ghs.en: That is what I decide it is.
ghs.assessment: The source asserts certainty that it must have been coincidence. The English instead describes a conscious personal decision to label it that way.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It had to be a coincidence.'

highlights.text: That is what I decide it is

rows.jp: でも、どうだろう。

ghs.en: But... was it?

rows.jp: 「このまま先輩と親しくしてたら、いけないのかも……だってそれは」
rows.en: “Maybe I shouldn’t keep getting this close to you... because—”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Getting close to you like this, Senpai, may just be wrong... because, after all,"

rows.jp: 言葉が途切れる。

ghs.en: Words interrupt.
ghs.assessment: The source says his words break off. The English uses an intransitive event with the wrong verb relation, suggesting that words interrupt something else.
ghs.remedy: Use 'My words break off.'

rows.jp: 静寂の夏。

ghs.en: A quiet, still summer.

rows.jp: あまりにも静かで、部活や授業の気配さえ消えていて。
rows.en: So silent that every trace of classes and club activities had vanished.

ghs.en: Excessively quiet, that even the signs of club activities and classes disappear.
ghs.assessment: The result construction is ungrammatical and shifts the surrounding past description into present tense. The source says it was so quiet that even signs of classes and club activity had vanished.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It was so quiet that even the sounds of classes and club activities had vanished.'

rows.jp: 静謐が支配する白い保健室。
rows.en: Stillness reigned over the white infirmary.

ghs.en: A white infirmary ruled by peace and quiet.

rows.jp: 世界が黄昏に満ちているのだから、白を基調とする室内は抗うことなく従属し、胎内に抱く二つの異物を生贄とばかりに夕暮れに差し出すはずだった。
rows.en: With the world steeped in twilight, the white room should have yielded without resistance, offering the two foreign bodies held in its womb as sacrifices to the dusk.

ghs.en: As the world was being filled by the dusk, the interior of the room with its white color as foundation would've subordinate it without a struggle, and offered to the twilight the two foreign elements held in it like would a womb, as scapegoats.
ghs.assessment: The clause is ungrammatical and assigns no coherent subject or object. The source imagines the white room yielding to dusk and offering up the two alien presences inside it like sacrifices.
ghs.remedy: Recast the sentence with the room as the subject that yields to dusk and offers up its two occupants.

rows.jp: 夕の色は、一日のどんな時間よりも印象に強い。
rows.en: No hour leaves an impression as powerful as evening.

ghs.en: The color of evening leaves an impression stronger than any other time of a day.
ghs.assessment: The English preserves the subject and comparison, but any other time of a day uses the wrong article pattern and is not idiomatic English.
ghs.remedy: Use any other time of day.

highlights.text: any other time of a day

rows.jp: すべてを異世界へと変えてしまう、おどろおどろしいもの。
rows.en: A sinister force that transforms everything into another world.

ghs.en: Everything changes into a parallel world, a thing of hair-raising eeriness.
ghs.assessment: The source calls evening an eerie thing that transforms everything into another world. The English instead makes everything transform itself and leaves the following apposition malformed.
ghs.remedy: Use 'An eerie force that turns everything into another world.'

highlights.text: Everything changes into a parallel world

rows.jp: 滅びの時間だ。

ghs.en: These are the hours of annihilation.
ghs.assessment: Annihilation is defensible for 滅び in this elevated passage, but the plural hours changes the source's singular compact image.
ghs.remedy: Use a singular hour or time of annihilation or ruin.

rows.jp: 世界が多重に見える時間。
rows.en: The hour when the world appears in layers.

ghs.en: Hours when the world can be seen in multiplex.
ghs.assessment: Multiplex retains the idea of multiplicity, but it is technical and nonidiomatic as a description of the world appearing layered; the plural hours also changes the source's singular time.
ghs.remedy: Describe a singular time when the world appears layered or multiple.

highlights.text: Hours when the world can be seen in multiplex

rows.jp: 沈んで、翌日また何食わぬ顔でやってきた大陽が昨日のそれと同一であると、誰が保証できるのか。
rows.en: Who could guarantee that the sun which sank, only to return the next day as if nothing had happened, was the same sun as before?

ghs.en: After it has sunk, who can possibly ascertain whether the sun that in the next day again comes full of nonchalance on its face is identical to the one of yesterday?
ghs.assessment: The embedded relative clause has malformed English word order. The source asks whether tomorrow's nonchalantly returning sun can be guaranteed to be yesterday's.
ghs.remedy: Use 'the sun that returns so nonchalantly the next day.'

highlights.text: that in the next day again comes

rows.jp: 毎日一回ずつ、世界が滅び去っているとしたら。
rows.en: Suppose the world perished once each day.

ghs.en: What if every day, one piece at a time, the world perishes and passes away.
ghs.assessment: The source says the world may perish once each day. The English mistakes the distributive count for gradual destruction piece by piece.
ghs.remedy: Use 'What if the world perishes once every day?'

rows.jp: 翌日とともに蘇生され、ただ人間だけがそれを知らないのだとしたら。
rows.en: Suppose it rose again with morning, and mankind alone remained unaware.

ghs.en: What if it is reborn along with the next day, and humans alone remain unaware.

rows.jp: 確認するすべはない。
rows.en: There would be no way to know.

ghs.en: There are no means to make sure.

rows.jp: 実際の世界と、人間の認識する世界が、同じだという保証はどこにもない。
rows.en: Nothing guaranteed that the world itself was the same as the world human beings perceived.

ghs.en: Nowhere there is proof that the world of reality and the world that humans are aware of are one and the same.
ghs.assessment: The negative locative requires inversion in this construction. The source says there is no guarantee anywhere that reality and human perception coincide.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Nowhere is there any proof...'

rows.jp: なのに今、ただ保健室の小空間だけが、緋色の侵攻から免れているように思えた。
rows.en: And yet this little pocket of the infirmary alone seemed spared the scarlet invasion.

ghs.en: And yet, right now, the small expanse of this ordinary infirmary alone appeared to be exempt from the invasion of brilliant scarlet.

rows.jp: いつになく、世界が鮮明に見ていたからだ。
rows.en: Because the world looked clearer than ever before.

ghs.en: Because, unusually, I had seen the world so clearly.
ghs.assessment: The source says the world looked unusually vivid or clear at that moment. The English turns appearance into a completed act of seeing in past perfect.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Because the world looked unusually vivid.'

rows.jp: 「……完璧な人なんて、どこにもいないじゃないですか？」
rows.en: “...There’s no such thing as a perfect person, is there?”

ghs.en: Misato: "...a perfect human does not exist anywhere, am I right?"

rows.jp: 「誰だって、どこかおかしいじゃないですか」

ghs.en: Misato: "Everybody is strange in some ways, am I right?"

rows.jp: 「いちいち欠点や失敗を攻撃していたら、生きていけないです」
rows.en: “We couldn’t live if we attacked every flaw and every mistake.”

ghs.en: Misato: "Attacking every single fault and mistake one by one is not the way to live."
ghs.assessment: The source says people could not go on living if they attacked every flaw and failure. The English weakens that consequence into general advice about a preferable way to live.
ghs.remedy: Use 'If we attacked every flaw and mistake, we couldn't live.'

highlights.text: is not the way to live

rows.jp: 「ねえ、そうでしょう？」

ghs.en: Misato: "Well? Do you agree?"
Taichi: "..."

rows.jp: 涙のひとつも出れば、格好悪く格好がつくのだが。
rows.en: A tear or two would at least have made my disgrace look presentable.

ghs.en: If I shed but a single tear, I'll look as cool as a tool.

rows.jp: 不思議と、激しい情動はなりをひそめていた。
rows.en: Strangely, though, the violent surge of emotion had fallen quiet.

ghs.en: Inexplicably, the extreme emotions have fallen silent.
ghs.assessment: The surrounding narration is simple past, and the source says the intense emotion had curiously gone quiet. The English present perfect breaks the narrative time frame.
ghs.remedy: Use 'the intense emotions had fallen silent.'

rows.jp: 「……一人だった俺を、部活に誘ってくれた先輩のことは、ソンケーしてるわけで」
rows.en: “...I really do look up to you, you know. You invited me to join the club when I was alone.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...when I was alone, and then you invited me to club, I... respect you so much for that."

rows.jp: 訥々(とつとつ)と話す俺。

ghs.en: Speaking in halting fragments,

rows.jp: 見守る先輩。

ghs.en: Senpai watching over me,

rows.jp: 静かに時間がうつろう。

ghs.en: while hours abate in the quiet.
ghs.assessment: The source says time passes quietly. 'Abate' means diminish in intensity and does not describe hours moving on.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Time passes quietly.'

rows.jp: 「嫌われるのは嫌だから、傷つけたくもなく」
rows.en: “I don’t want you to hate me. I don’t want to hurt you, either.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I don't want to be disliked, so I don't want to hurt anyone either."
ghs.assessment: The source coordinates two personal fears: being disliked and hurting the addressee. The English makes the second a result of the first and broadens its object to anyone.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I don't want to be disliked, and I don't want to hurt you.'

highlights.text: so I don't want to hurt anyone

rows.jp: 「……さっきのことは申し訳ないと思っていて」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...I think that what I did right then is unforgivable."
ghs.assessment: The source says he feels sorry or remorseful about what happened. Calling the act unforgivable intensifies the moral judgment and changes the confession's stance.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I feel terrible about what happened earlier.'

rows.jp: 「でも自制する自信はなくて」
rows.en: “But I can’t trust myself to stay in control.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But I have no self-confidence in my self-control."
ghs.assessment: The doubled abstract noun phrase is an unnatural calque. The source says he lacks confidence that he can restrain himself.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I'm not confident I can control myself.'

rows.jp: 「どうすればいいですか？」

ghs.en: Misato: "So what can we do?"
Taichi: "Eh?"

rows.jp: 「まずどこに気をつけたらいいんです？　わたしとしては」
rows.en: “Then what should I watch out for first?”

ghs.en: Misato: "First of all, what is there to be careful about? As for myself, I mean."

rows.jp: 「……それは」

ghs.en: Taichi: "...well."

rows.jp: 冷静に考えれば。

ghs.en: If I think with composure,

rows.jp: 「先輩の血を見ないようにすれば」
rows.en: “If I can keep from seeing your blood...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "If I make sure not to see your blood, Senpai..."

rows.jp: 「怪我に気をつけろってことですね？」
rows.en: “So I should be careful not to hurt myself?”

ghs.en: Misato: "So I should be careful not to get hurt?"

rows.jp: 「はい」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yes."

rows.jp: 「でもわたしはアンテナを組み立てたり、工具使ったり、怪我をする危険に面している」
rows.en: “But I build antennas and use tools. That puts me at risk of getting hurt.”

ghs.en: Misato: "But I am putting the antenna together, and using tools, so I really face the risk of injuries."

rows.jp: 「はい、だから俺がそばにいない方が」
rows.en: “Right. Which is why I shouldn’t be near you—”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Yes, therefore, me not being near you..."

rows.jp: 「ぺけくんが」

ghs.en: Misato: "But, Peke-kun..."

rows.jp: 遮って、言った。

ghs.en: Interjected, this she said:
ghs.assessment: The inversion is unidiomatic and leaves the participle without a clear subject. The source says she cut him off and spoke.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She cut me off and said,'

rows.jp: 「力仕事を手伝ってくれるんでしょう？」
rows.en: “You’ll be helping me with the heavy lifting, won’t you?”

ghs.en: Misato: "Would you help me with the heavy lifting?"
ghs.assessment: The source is a confident confirmation that he will help with the heavy work, not a tentative future request. The English weakens her decisive interruption.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You'll help me with the heavy lifting, won't you?'

rows.jp: 効いた。

ghs.en: That worked.

rows.jp: じんわりと、肋骨に包まれた胸の奥を、震わせた。
rows.en: Slowly, it sent a tremor through the heart behind my ribs.

ghs.en: Gradually, the depth enclosed by the ribs of my cage were made to quiver.
ghs.assessment: The English has number disagreement and invents a separate cage possessing ribs. The source says her words slowly made the depths of his rib-enclosed chest tremble.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Slowly, they made something deep inside my rib cage tremble.'

highlights.text: the depth enclosed by the ribs of my cage were made to quiver

rows.jp: 『いつもお一人なんですね』

ghs.en: 『You are always alone, are you.』
ghs.assessment: The English tag question is malformed and punctuated as a statement. The source observes that he is always alone and seeks confirmation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You're always alone, aren't you?'

rows.jp: 『一緒に、部活しませんか？』
rows.en: “Would you like to join the club with me?”

ghs.en: 『Will you not have club together with me?』
ghs.assessment: The phrase is not idiomatic English and obscures the invitation to do club activities together.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Would you like to join me in the club?'

rows.jp: 心の中の語録に、一つ、加えられたその言葉は。
rows.en: Those words became one more entry in the private book of quotations inside me.

ghs.en: Those words had been added, as one quote, in the anthology deep inside my heart.

rows.jp: 圧倒的にあたたかく、やわらかく、力強かった。
rows.en: It was overwhelmingly warm. Soft. Strong.

ghs.en: Overwhelmingly warm, overwhelmingly soft, overwhelmingly strong.

rows.jp: 自分一人では解決できない悩みを、他人のたった一言が解消してしまう。
rows.en: A single word from someone else can solve a problem you could never solve alone.

ghs.en: When I have worry that I cannot resolve alone, a single solitary word from another erases it.
ghs.assessment: The singular count noun lacks an article, and the construction needlessly turns the source's general statement into a temporal subordinate clause.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A single word from someone else can erase a worry I cannot solve alone.'

rows.jp: そのために、人は互いに通じ合いたいと思うのだった。
rows.en: That is why people long to reach one another.

ghs.en: I believed that people desire reciprocal communication is for the sake of that.
ghs.assessment: The English is syntactically incoherent and adds a first-person belief frame. The source concludes that this is why people want to understand and connect with one another.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That is why people want to connect with one another.'

highlights.text: I believed that people desire reciprocal communication is for the sake of that

rows.jp: 言葉で、体で、携帯で。
rows.en: Through words, through bodies, through phones.

ghs.en: With words, with the body, with cellphones.

rows.jp: ……通信で。

ghs.en: ...with intercommunication.

rows.jp: ありとあらゆる手段で。

ghs.en: In every single way, with all possible means.

rows.jp: 触れあおうと努力できる。
rows.en: We can strive to make contact.

ghs.en: A desire for reciprocal touch accomplished through great effort:
ghs.assessment: The source says people are capable of striving to reach or touch one another. The English changes ability and continuing effort into a desire already accomplished.
ghs.remedy: Use 'We can strive to reach one another.'

highlights.text: A desire for reciprocal touch accomplished through great effort

rows.jp: それが人だ。
rows.en: That is what it means to be human.

ghs.en: that is a Person.

rows.jp: 「やっぱり組み立て、手伝ってもらうことにします」
rows.en: “I’ve decided I do want your help putting it together.”

ghs.en: Misato: "I knew it, I ended up needing to ask for help for the assembly."
ghs.assessment: The source says she has decided after all to have him help. The English recasts that choice as an externally imposed need.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I've decided to have you help me assemble it after all.'

highlights.text: I ended up needing to ask

ghs.en: Taichi: "...yes ma'am."

rows.jp: 気恥ずかしい。

ghs.en: I feel ashamed.
ghs.assessment: The source describes self-conscious embarrassment or bashfulness, not moral shame. The English gives the feeling an unjustified ethical weight.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I feel bashful.'

rows.jp: 先輩はにこにこと楽しそう。

ghs.en: Senpai smiles bright, looking like she's enjoying herself.
ghs.assessment: The verb requires an adverb in this construction. The source describes Senpai smiling brightly and looking pleased.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Senpai smiles brightly.'

rows.jp: 曜子さんは、俺のことを強力な人間だと言った。
rows.en: Youko had called me a powerful person.

ghs.en: Youko-chan said that I make for a very strong human being.
ghs.assessment: The source uses the respectful adult address 'Youko-san.' The English changes it to the diminutive intimate suffix '-chan.'
ghs.remedy: Use 'Youko-san.'

rows.jp: そういう価値の認め方は、好きじゃない。
rows.en: I didn’t like being valued that way.

ghs.en: But I don't like the way she recognizes that value.

rows.jp: 違う。

ghs.en: It's wrong.

rows.jp: 俺以外の人間は、えてして凄い。
rows.en: It was everyone else who was incredible.

ghs.en: Humans outside of me are so often amazing.
ghs.assessment: Humans outside of me is intelligible by calque, but in English it suggests people physically outside the speaker rather than people other than him.
ghs.remedy: Use other people or everyone but me.

rows.jp: いつだってみみ先輩は、俺をいい気にさせたり手玉にとったり魅惑したりする。
rows.en: Mimi could always make me feel like a king, play me like a fiddle, and leave me spellbound.

ghs.en: Any time anywhere Mimi-senpai can make me feel pleasant and lead me by the nose and captivate me.

rows.jp: そんなこと……自分ではできない。
rows.en: I could never do any of that myself.

ghs.en: That is something... that cannot be done on one's own.
ghs.assessment: The source is a first-person admission that he cannot do those things himself. The English generalizes it into an impersonal universal claim.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I could never do those things myself.'

highlights.text: cannot be done on one's own

rows.jp: そばにいたい。
rows.en: I wanted to stay beside her.

ghs.en: I want to be beside her,

rows.jp: 時が許す日まで。
rows.en: For as long as time would allow.

ghs.en: until the day that time allows,

rows.jp: 終わりの日まで。

ghs.en: until the day that is the end,

rows.jp: そしてまだ、時間はあるのだ。

ghs.en: and even then, there will be time.
ghs.assessment: The source affirms that there is still time now. The English shifts it to a future after the previously named end point and adds 'even then,' reversing the temporal relation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'And there is still time.'

highlights.text: even then, there will be time

rows.jp: 「おねがいします」

ghs.en: Taichi: "It will be my pleasure."
Misato: "Hmmm."

rows.jp: 頭を下げて、

ghs.en: With a bow of her head,
ghs.assessment: The source's implicit subject is the narrator, who bows his head. The English assigns the bow to Senpai and reverses the action immediately before she touches him.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I bow my head,'

rows.jp: 先輩の手がぽんと置かれて、
rows.en: and her hand settled gently upon it,

ghs.en: Senpai makes her hands fall together with a pof,
ghs.assessment: The source says Senpai places one hand lightly on him. The English makes plural hands fall together, suggesting a clap and omitting the contact.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Senpai's hand comes to rest lightly on me,'

rows.jp: こそばゆくて、

ghs.en: awkwardly,
ghs.assessment: The source describes a ticklish, pleasantly bashful sensation. 'Awkwardly' describes manner rather than the narrator's tactile and emotional response.
ghs.remedy: Use 'feeling pleasantly ticklish,'

rows.jp: やっと笑えて、
rows.en: until at last I could smile.

ghs.en: eventually smiling,
ghs.assessment: The source says the narrator was finally able to smile. The participial English omits ability and leaves the subject implicit.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I can finally smile,'

rows.jp: これで、もとどおり。
rows.en: Just like that, everything was back to normal.

ghs.en: and with that, she is as she was.
ghs.assessment: The source leaves the restored state implicit: 'With that, back to normal.' The English specifically asserts that Senpai herself is restored, despite the sequence centering the narrator and their relationship.
ghs.remedy: Preserve the open reference with 'And with that, everything is back to normal.'

rows.jp: 涙が出るほど嬉しかった。
rows.en: I was so happy I could have cried.

ghs.en: I was so happy I felt tears coming.

rows.jp: 先輩の手が、カーテンをあける。

ghs.en: Senpai's hands open the curtains.
ghs.assessment: The source names a single hand. The English pluralizes it without support.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Senpai's hand opens the curtain.'

rows.jp: 一瞬で、保健室はオレンジ色に食べられた。
rows.en: In an instant, the infirmary was devoured by orange.

ghs.en: In one instant the infirmary was devoured by the orange.
